title: Cyber Security Engineer Salary Australia 2026
metaDescription: Cyber security engineer salary in Australia 2026: average pay, junior to senior ranges, top-paying cities and certifications that lift your salary.
headline: Cyber Security Engineer Salary Australia 2026

sections.title: How Much Do Cyber Security Engineers Earn in 2026?
sections.content:
Cyber security engineers in Australia earn an average of around AUD 117,000 to AUD 134,000 per year in 2026, depending on the source. Indeed reports an average of AUD 133,738 from 136 salaries, while Jobicy puts the average at AUD 116,900. The typical range runs from about AUD 96,000 to AUD 186,000.

By seniority, juniors earn AUD 70,000 to AUD 100,000, mid-level engineers AUD 105,000 to AUD 140,000, and seniors AUD 140,000 to AUD 175,000. Security architects earn AUD 155,000 to AUD 217,000, and CISOs can exceed AUD 300,000. Demand is very high, with about 25 percent annual growth.

sections.title: Where the Pay Is Highest
sections.content:
Financial services, government, defence, and critical infrastructure pay the most, with some specialists in Sydney finance and defence clearing AUD 190,000 or more. Companies are paying up to a 19 percent premium above standard senior engineering rates just to fill these roles.

Sydney and Melbourne offer the highest salaries, while Canberra pays well for cleared defence and government roles. Contract work is lucrative too: security engineers command AUD 800 to AUD 1,200 per day, with cloud security specialists at AUD 900 to AUD 1,200 per day.

sections.title: Certifications That Raise Your Salary
sections.content:
The most in-demand certifications in 2025-2026 are CISSP, CISM, AWS Security Specialty, and AZ-500 for Microsoft Azure Security. AI and ML security specialisations now pay 25 to 40 percent above base security salaries, reflecting the surge in demand for engineers who can secure AI systems.

Australia's 2023-2030 Cyber Security Strategy has made the field one of the most consistently in-demand specialisations in IT. The Australian Signals Directorate's Essential Eight framework is now a common benchmark employers expect engineers to know and apply.

sections.title: Career Path and Getting In
sections.content:
A typical path runs from security analyst to security engineer, then senior engineer, architect, and eventually CISO or head of security. Hands-on skills in cloud security, network defence, incident response, and scripting matter more than degrees alone.

To enter the field, build a foundation in networking and Linux, earn a respected certification, and practise in home labs or capture-the-flag competitions. Employers value demonstrated skills, and the shortage of experienced engineers means strong juniors can progress quickly.
